input.heading: More particles, not faster particles
input.lead: Doubling concentration at the same temperature does not make particles move faster.
points: Successful collisions need enough energy to react.
More particles mean more collisions each second, not more energy per collision.

diagram.shows: Two equal-volume acid samples at 20°C beside identical magnesium surfaces. One has twice as many acid particles as the other. Both show the same distribution of movement-arrow lengths, demonstrating unchanged typical speed.

slide.heading: More particles, not faster particles
slide.lead: Doubling concentration at the same temperature does not make particles move faster.
points: Compare equal volumes of dilute and concentrated acid at 20°C with identical magnesium surfaces; the concentrated acid has twice as many acid particles.
Successful collisions need enough energy to react.
Both samples have the same distribution of particle speeds. More particles mean more collisions each second, not more energy per collision.
